text:
emma: Heads-up — we're seeing a drop in 'enablement_completed' events feeding the CRM. AMs report completed trainings not reflecting in customer playbooks and renewal-risk bumped for some cohorts.

rafael: Observed same. Looks like the enablement feedback form webhook returned 401s starting ~03:10 UTC. Example payload id=FB-9921 status=401 token_invalid.

cs-bot: webhook-monitor alert: enablement-webhook 401 spike at 03:10 UTC (+412 errors) :warning:

nina: I checked the logs: webhook receiver `cs-webhooks/prod` rejected requests after token rotate deployed this morning. The new secret name is `enablement-v2` while the form still posts old header `X-CS-TOKEN: enablement-legacy`.

jared (eng): Confirmed. During secrets rollout we accidentally deprecated `enablement-legacy` without adding a backwards-compatible alias. I can add an auth shim to accept both tokens for 48h. PR: https://git.redwood/s/cs/webhooks/+/2876 (auth shim + test).

sam (product): How many accounts affected? AMs say 50+ show 'training complete' in LMS but not in CRM. That means playbook automation didn't mark onboarding as complete and healthscore penalized recency.

amanda: Here's a quick SQL to find mismatches: `SELECT acct_id FROM lms_submissions WHERE status='completed' AND acct_id NOT IN (SELECT acct_id FROM crm_events WHERE event_type='enablement_completed' AND ts > now()-30d)` — yields 54 rows for cohort `enterprise-q3`.

emma: Can we do two things: 1) reingest missed events once the shim is live 2) add a playbook guard to ignore missing enablement events for 48h after token rotate to avoid false negatives?

jared (eng): For reingest I can replay webhooks from our delivery logs. Steps: enable shim, replay logs with `replay_webhooks.py --filter token=enablement-legacy --dry-run` then commit. Dry-run path: s3://redwood-cs/replays/1759999001/dry.csv

cs-bot: replayer queued 54 events for dry-run.

nina: I also recommend patching the playbook: add `tolerance_window` config for critical signals. For enablement flags set tolerance_window=72h so short outages don't flip account state. I'll open a config PR.

amanda: On AM comms: I'll draft a message apologizing and explaining reingest + what we'll do to prevent recurrence. Also will include a CSV of impacted accounts.

sam (product): Long term, let's add a webhook health dashboard and a token-rotation runbook: 1) rotate secret 2) create alias 3) enable shim 4) test on staging 5) gradual rotate 6) rollback plan. I'll write the runbook and link it to ops docs.

jared (eng): Rolling the shim to prod now. After deploy I'll kick the dry-run replay and share results.

cs-bot: deploy cs-webhooks v1.23.1 started by jared at 04:02 UTC

jared (eng): Deploy successful. Running dry-run replay now. Command:

```
python tools/replay_webhooks.py --env prod --filter token=enablement-legacy --dry-run --out s3://redwood-cs/replays/1759999001/dry.csv
```

Will post counts.

cs-bot: replay dry-run completed: candidate=54, would_ingest=54, sample_out s3://redwood-cs/replays/1759999001/dry.csv

emma: Great. After proper run, please mark these events as backfilled and trigger playbook rerun for impacted accounts. Also, nina please set tolerance_window=72h and add to config: `playbook.stalled_onboard.tolerance.enablement=72h`.

nina: Added config PR: https://git.redwood/s/cs/config/+/901 (includes tests). Will patch staging first.

amanda: Drafted AM note and uploaded account CSV to shared drive. Will ping once reingest complete.

jared (eng): Starting actual replay now (non-dry-run).

cs-bot: replay started by jared 04:20 UTC -> processed=54 successes=54 failures=0

emma: Thanks all. Follow-ups: jared please keep the shim for 48h then rotate tokens with aliasing. sam please add runbook link to the rotation timeline. nina please monitor health for 72h to ensure no further misses. Amanda will send AM note in 30m.

sam (product): I'll own the runbook and schedule a retro on the rollout process. Also we'll add an automated smoke test post-rotation.

amanda: AM note sent. Two AM replies so far, both appreciative.

emma: Closing the loop — great cross-team work. Let's capture this in a short incident postmortem and tag action items.
